items.title: EventRecord index is a materialized launch-critical canonical MessagePack index
items.statement: The event_record_index family is a materialized tier-0 redb index keyed by project, sequence, and event identity, encoded canonically as MessagePack, with a fixed schema identifier and version.

items.title: EventRecord index values have a closed required-field schema
items.statement: EventRecord index values reject additional properties; require identity, location, payload hash, idempotency, correlation, persistence time, and redaction fields; and permit causation_event_id as the sole optional nullable field.

items.title: EventRecord index is rebuildable and points to authoritative seglog bytes
items.statement: Replay follows the index back to authoritative seglog bytes, orders by segment generation, segment order, offset, and sequence_id, and allows index compaction only when authoritative seglog retention permits it.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Index row points back to authoritative seglog bytes and is rebuildable; replay ordering uses segment generation, segment order, offset, and sequence_id.",
"retention_compaction": "Rebuildable index may compact only after authoritative seglog retention permits it.",

items.title: EventRecord index ownership and dataflow are named
items.statement: The storage plan owns the persistence boundary, the seglog EventRecord projector produces the index, and idempotency replay, audit lookup, and projectors consume it.

items.title: Blocked projection is a materialized launch-critical project-node projection
items.statement: The blocked_projection family is a materialized tier-0 redb projection keyed canonically by project_id and node_id with a fixed schema identity, version, and canonical MessagePack encoding.

items.title: Blocked projection ownership, producer, and consumers are named
items.statement: The storage-plan migration/versioning rule owns the family, the Executor blocked-state projector produces it, and the Planning Wizard, Orchestrator, and Goal Runtime consume it.

items.title: Blocked projection exposes freshness and health state vocabularies
items.statement: Freshness is one of current, stale, rebuilding, or unavailable; health is one of healthy, degraded, or unavailable; both are required alongside blocked identity, reason, source events, timestamps, and redaction profile.

items.title: Blocked projection rebuild and mutation guard behavior is explicit for stale or degraded states
items.statement: The projection rebuilds from EventRecord or receipt sources, and stale or degraded projections must block mutation-capable actions.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Projection rebuilds from EventRecord/receipt sources; stale or degraded projections block mutation-capable actions.",

items.title: Legacy blocked keys are read aliases while canonical writes use the v1 project-node key
items.statement: Migration compatibility is intentionally one-way: run-scoped legacy keys remain readable aliases, while new writes target the canonical v1 project/node key.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Run-scoped blocked_projection.{run_id}.{node_id}.{blocked_sequence} keys are migration-read aliases only; canonical writes use v1 project/node key.",

items.title: Replay ordering names segment components absent from the value contract
items.statement: Replay ordering requires segment generation and segment order, but the value schema exposes only segment_ref, byte_offset, and sequence_id and does not define how generation or order is derived from segment_ref.
items.impact: Independent builders can derive different replay order from the same rows, threatening deterministic replay and audit lookup.
items.builder_discretion: The builder must invent a segment_ref grammar or an out-of-band lookup for segment generation and segment order.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Index row points back to authoritative seglog bytes and is rebuildable; replay ordering uses segment generation, segment order, offset, and sequence_id.",

items.title: payload_sha256 is not validated as a SHA-256 digest
items.statement: The field is named payload_sha256 but its schema accepts any non-empty string; no hexadecimal alphabet or 64-character length is required.
items.impact: Malformed or non-SHA-256 values can satisfy the registry schema and undermine integrity checks.
items.builder_discretion: Each producer or consumer must decide whether and how to validate digest syntax.

items.title: Nullable causation identity permits an empty string
items.statement: causation_event_id allows string or null but imposes no minimum length on the string alternative, unlike other identity fields.
items.impact: An empty string can become a third effective absence representation alongside null and omission.
items.builder_discretion: Consumers must decide whether empty string means absent, invalid, or a real identifier.

items.title: Event index no-secret prose conflicts with the declared stored fields
items.statement: The rule says the index stores only ids, offsets, hashes, and refs, while the required schema also stores event_type, persisted_at_utc, and redaction_profile; the intended meaning of only is therefore inconsistent with the contract.
items.impact: Privacy review and export filtering cannot determine whether non-listed metadata is authorized or violates the no-secret rule.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose whether the prose is illustrative or an exhaustive allowlist.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "Index stores only ids, offsets, hashes, and refs; payload bytes stay in seglog under EventRecord redaction rules.",

items.title: Projection state sets lack transition and precedence rules
items.statement: The freshness and health enums define possible values but not legal transitions, which state owns action gating when the two dimensions disagree, or whether timestamp updates must be atomic with state changes.
items.impact: Projectors and consumers can disagree on valid state sequences and on whether mutation is safe.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent a two-dimensional state machine, transition legality, precedence, and update atomicity.

items.title: Mutation gating omits explicit semantics for rebuilding and unavailable
items.statement: The behavior expressly blocks mutations for stale freshness or degraded health, but the enums also include rebuilding and unavailable without stating whether those states fail closed.
items.impact: A consumer may permit mutation while its projection is rebuilding or unavailable.
items.builder_discretion: Consumers must decide independently whether unmentioned non-current states block or permit mutation.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Projection rebuilds from EventRecord/receipt sources; stale or degraded projections block mutation-capable actions.",

items.title: Recovery target exists without recovery or unblock semantics
items.statement: recovery_target_ref is optional and nullable, but no behavior defines who writes it, how it is interpreted, what succeeds or fails recovery, or when a blocked projection is cleared.
items.impact: A blocked node can lack a deterministic recovery path or remain inconsistently blocked across consumers.
items.builder_discretion: The implementation must invent recovery target resolution, authorization, completion evidence, and unblock transitions.

items.title: Blocked reason vocabulary and GUI disabled-reason mapping are unspecified
items.statement: blocked_reason_code and blocked_family accept arbitrary non-empty strings, while the Planning Wizard consumes a disabled reason; no stable vocabulary, localization key, fallback, precedence, or mapping is defined.
items.impact: The GUI, Orchestrator, and Goal Runtime can present or classify the same block differently and cannot rely on exhaustive handling.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent reason codes and the user-visible mapping and fallback policy.

items.title: Required source-event traceability can be empty or contain empty identifiers
items.statement: source_event_ids is required, but its array has no minItems and its string items have no minLength, so the schema admits zero usable provenance events.
items.impact: Blocked receipts and rebuilt projections can satisfy the schema without auditable source-event evidence.
items.builder_discretion: Producers and validators must decide whether at least one non-empty event identifier is mandatory.

items.title: Optional collection and nullable-field absence semantics are undefined
items.statement: approval_scope_key and recovery_target_ref may be absent or null, while optional arrays may be absent or empty; the contract does not define whether these representations are semantically equivalent.
items.impact: Canonical encoding, equality, projection diffs, and consumer branching can diverge for semantically similar records.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose normalization rules for absent, null, and empty values.

items.title: File-path redaction has no machine-readable representation or validator
items.statement: The prose permits redacted or ref-only file paths and invalidates raw secret content, but dirty_file_paths and conflict_file_paths are unconstrained strings with no schema marker for redacted versus raw form.
items.impact: Sensitive paths or credentials can pass schema validation and consumers cannot distinguish safe refs from raw paths.
items.builder_discretion: Implementations must invent redaction syntax, detection, export behavior, and rejection rules.

evidence.exact_quote: "redaction_no_secret_rule": "File paths may be redacted or ref-only under export policy; raw secret content and credentials are invalid.",

items.title: Legacy alias resolution and retirement are unspecified
items.statement: The migration contract permits legacy read aliases and canonical v1 writes but does not define precedence when both exist, collision handling across run-scoped rows, migration completion evidence, or alias retirement.
items.impact: Readers can return different blocked state or preserve aliases indefinitely, complicating compaction and correctness.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose merge precedence, deduplication, conflict resolution, and deprecation timing.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Run-scoped blocked_projection.{run_id}.{node_id}.{blocked_sequence} keys are migration-read aliases only; canonical writes use v1 project/node key.",

items.title: Retention and compaction depend on unnamed operational authority and thresholds
items.statement: The event index compacts when seglog retention permits it, and blocked sources retain according to receipt or audit policy, but neither condition identifies the deciding actor, concrete policy reference, threshold, trigger, or completion oracle.
items.impact: Operators cannot deterministically know when data may be compacted or must be retained.
items.builder_discretion: The implementation must select policy sources, authority boundaries, schedules, and safe-compaction checks.

evidence.exact_quote: "retention_compaction": "Rebuildable index may compact only after authoritative seglog retention permits it.",
"retention_compaction": "Projection is rebuildable, but source events and blocked receipts retain according to receipt/audit policy.",

items.title: Collection and string sizes are unbounded
items.statement: The blocked projection allows unbounded source events, allowed actions, dirty paths, and conflict paths, with unconstrained item lengths; the launch-critical schema provides no record-size or cardinality limits.
items.impact: Projection records can grow without a portable bound, affecting storage, canonical encoding, rebuild time, and GUI consumption.
items.builder_discretion: Implementations must choose truncation, pagination, maximum cardinality, maximum string length, and overflow behavior.

items.title: Producer-to-consumer propagation timing and consistency are unspecified
items.statement: The registry names projectors and consumers but defines no freshness deadline, update ordering, notification mechanism, atomicity, or consumer behavior while a newer blocked event is not yet projected.
items.impact: The Planning Wizard, Orchestrator, and Goal Runtime can observe different blocked truth and authorize inconsistent actions.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose propagation semantics, staleness bounds, and read-after-write guarantees.

items.title: Structural schemas do not provide semantic acceptance oracles
items.statement: The schemas can validate field shape and enum membership, but this window defines no executable oracle for replay order, rebuild equivalence, fail-closed mutation gating, alias migration, redaction compliance, or recovery completion.
items.impact: Conformant-looking implementations can differ on launch-critical behavior without a decisive acceptance test.
items.builder_discretion: Builders and reviewers must invent fixtures and semantic pass/fail criteria.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Index row points back to authoritative seglog bytes and is rebuildable; replay ordering uses segment generation, segment order, offset, and sequence_id.",
"replay_behavior": "Projection rebuilds from EventRecord/receipt sources; stale or degraded projections block mutation-capable actions.",

items.title: Composite key component encoding is not defined
items.statement: Both key shapes interpolate string identifiers using colon separators, but the contract does not define escaping, normalization, byte encoding, or whether identifiers containing colons are valid.
items.impact: Different encoders can create collisions or fail to resolve the same logical key.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose component normalization and separator escaping rules.

items.title: EventEnvelope migration metadata is named but not contracted
items.statement: The migration says legacy rows add migration metadata at EventRecord level, but this index value schema neither names those metadata fields nor defines migration version, idempotence, failure handling, or completion evidence.
items.impact: Migrators cannot produce a uniquely testable upgraded record or prove that all legacy rows were converted safely.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent metadata shape and migration execution and verification semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: "migration": "Legacy EventEnvelopeV1 lookup rows migrate by adding schema_id/schema_version/event_type and migration metadata at EventRecord level.",

dimension_assessments.summary: The window specifies index replay and compaction behavior plus blocked-projection rebuild and mutation gating behavior.
It defines materialized lookup and blocked-state projection capabilities that are rebuildable from authoritative sources.
Composite key shapes, producers, consumers, required values, optional values, and encoded object shapes are named.
Closed schemas exist, but replay inputs, digest validation, key serialization, and migration metadata remain under-contracted.
Freshness and health state values are enumerated, but their legal transitions, precedence, atomicity, and recovery transitions are not.
Document ownership and producer roles are named, but retention, compaction, mutation gating for unmentioned states, and recovery authorities are not fully assigned.
Each family names an owner document and a producing projector.
The event index and blocked projection each enumerate their downstream consumers.
The Planning Wizard disabled-reason consumer is named, but reason-code vocabulary and user-visible mapping behavior are absent.
Stale or degraded projections block mutation, but unavailable and rebuilding semantics plus recovery and unblock behavior are incomplete.
No-secret and redaction prose exists, but the event allowlist is internally inconsistent and blocked file-path redaction is not machine-enforced.
Producer and consumer topology is named without timing, consistency, notification, or read-after-write guarantees.
Replay, rebuild, migration, retention, and compaction are described, but their triggers, authority, recovery, and completion evidence are incomplete.
Canonical MessagePack and compactable rebuildable storage help performance, but record sizes and collection cardinalities have no bounds.
Both families name legacy migration behavior, but alias resolution, retirement, metadata, idempotence, and migration proof are under-specified.
Structural JSON-schema validation is available, but launch-critical semantic behavior lacks executable acceptance oracles.
Consequential discretion remains in ordering derivation, state machines, fail-closed behavior, recovery, GUI mapping, redaction, migration, retention, scale, and propagation.
Unknowns include absent/null/empty equivalence, key escaping, replay component derivation, unavailable-state behavior, and migration completion semantics.
